summary: This work proposes a Purcell-engineered hybrid coupler architecture for superconducting CZ gates that combines a nonlinear transmon coupler with a coupled Purcell-filter and notch-resonator subsystem to engineer both coherent interactions and leakage-selective dissipation. The optimized gate achieves $F_{m avg}=99.74	exttt{%}$, $F_{m min}=99.62	exttt{%}$, and maximum leakage of $1.6	imes10^{-3}$, reducing leakage nearly twentyfold compared to an optimized single-transmon coupler.
motivation: Leakage into non-computational states has become increasingly detrimental to superconducting quantum error correction as coherent control errors decrease; existing mitigation strategies rely primarily on pulse shaping and coherent interaction engineering, leaving engineered dissipation relatively unexplored as a complementary tool for selective leakage suppression.
method: The architecture integrates a nonlinear transmon coupler with a lossy Purcell-filter resonator (coupled to a 50 Ω environment at rate $\kappa_f/2\pi=2.0$ MHz) and a weakly dissipative notch resonator ($\kappa_n/2\pi=0.02$ MHz) that together reshape the frequency-dependent electromagnetic environment. Gate performance is evaluated using dressed-eigenstate analysis and Lindblad master-equation simulations across multiple coherence sets.
result: Compared to an optimized single-transmon coupler, the hybrid architecture reduces maximum leakage from $3\times10^{-2}$ to $1.6\times10^{-3}$ while improving minimum computational-state fidelity from $0.976$ to $0.9962$, with the gate duration extending from 257 ns to 327.3 ns; robustness scans show high-fidelity, low-leakage operation persists over broad ranges of filter frequency ($\omega_f/2\pi\approx3.9$ GHz), filter–coupler coupling ($g_{cf}/2\pi\approx92.5$ MHz), and qubit–filter couplings ($g_{1f}/2\pi\approx5.8$ MHz, $g_{2f}/2\pi\approx6.7$ MHz).
